terminal.description: The screen runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. This shell opens in your workspace in case you want to look around.

tasks.title: Keep the chosen tram in TramGuide and hand it down
tasks.description:
Take the chosen tram out of `TramList` and `TramPanel`, and keep it in one place: state in `TramGuide`, holding the chosen tram's `number`, starting with the first tram of `trams`.

- `TramList({ trams, chosen })` marks the button of the tram whose number is `chosen` with `aria-pressed`, and keeps no state of its own.
- `TramPanel({ tram })` shows the tram it is given, and keeps no state of its own.
- `TramGuide` hands `chosen` to the list and the chosen tram object to the panel.

Pressing does nothing for now; the next two tasks bring it back. The check draws `TramList` and `TramPanel` on their own with trams of its own, changes their props, and looks at what they show. Then it draws `TramGuide` and looks at the list and the panel.
nextSteps: Read "Two copies disagree" and "Move the state up" in the lesson.
Add the state to `TramGuide`, and work out the chosen tram object from it.
Give `TramList` a `chosen` prop and `TramPanel` a `tram` prop, and remove their own state.
Change the starting number in the Browser panel and watch both follow.
hints: Two pieces of state that should always be equal are one too many. Keep one, in the component that draws both.
`useState` moves to `TramGuide`. The list compares each tram's number with its `chosen` prop; the panel draws whatever `tram` prop it gets. `find` gives the tram object for a number.

In `TramGuide`: `const [chosen, setChosen] = useState(trams[0].number)` and `const tram = trams.find((t) => t.number === chosen)`, then `<TramList trams={trams} chosen={chosen} />` and `<TramPanel tram={tram} />`.

tasks.title: Choose a tram from the list
tasks.description:
Give `TramList` an `onChoose` prop. Pressing a tram's button calls `onChoose` once with that tram's `number`. The list does not move its own mark: the mark only follows `chosen`. `TramGuide` hands the list a function that sets its state, so the list and the panel move together.

The check draws `TramList` alone with an `onChoose` of its own that writes down each call and changes nothing, and presses trams. Then it draws `TramGuide` and presses trams in the list, looking at the list and the panel after each press.
nextSteps: Read "Changes travel up" in the lesson.
Take `onChoose` in `TramList`, and call it from each button with the tram's number.
Hand `TramList` an `onChoose` from `TramGuide` that sets the chosen number.
Press trams in the Browser panel and watch the panel follow.
hints: The list cannot change `chosen` itself: it is a prop. It can only tell its owner what was pressed.
The button calls `onChoose` with the tram's number, wrapped in an arrow so nothing is called while drawing. The setter itself is a fine function to hand down.
`onClick={() => onChoose(tram.number)}` in the list, and `<TramList trams={trams} chosen={chosen} onChoose={setChosen} />` in `TramGuide`.

tasks.title: Move to the next tram from the panel
tasks.description:
Give `TramPanel` an `onNext` prop, and call it when Next tram is pressed. The panel does not know the other trams, so `TramGuide` does the moving: it hands the panel a function that sets the chosen tram to the one after it in `trams`, and after the last tram comes the first.

The check draws `TramPanel` alone with an `onNext` of its own and presses Next tram. Then it draws `TramGuide` with trams of its own, presses Next tram once for each of them, and looks at the panel and the list after each press.
nextSteps: Read "Changes travel up" again, then "One source of truth".
Call `onNext` from the panel's Next tram button.
Move the work of `next` into `TramGuide`, so it changes `TramGuide`'s state.
Press Next tram past the last tram in the Browser panel.
hints: Whoever owns the state is the one who changes it. The panel only says that Next was pressed.
The starter's `next` function already does the moving; it just lives in the wrong component. `% trams.length` turns the index after the last into 0.

In `TramGuide`: `function next() { const at = trams.indexOf(tram); setChosen(trams[(at + 1) % trams.length].number) }`, then `<TramPanel tram={tram} onNext={next} />`, and `onClick={onNext}` on the button.
